scenes.label: Meet Meera
scenes.title: Waiting for the result
scenes.caption: Meera's scholarship interview went well, and now she checks her inbox every hour. Every real message so far has come from the Young Scientists office, youngscientists.cyberpur.example: the interview time, then a thank-you note. Today, a new email arrives with the office's logo and a subject that makes his heart jump.

Every real message so far has come from the Young Scientists office, youngscientists dot cyberpur dot example: the interview time, then a thank-you note. Today, a new email arrives with the office's logo and a subject that makes his heart jump.

scenes.label: The award email
scenes.title: “Pay within 24 hours.”
scenes.caption: Congratulations, it says. You have won an award! Submit your Aadhaar number and a ₹500 processing fee within 24 hours, or the award goes to someone else. The display name says Scholarship Office, and the logo looks right. Meera's finger hovers over Pay fee. But the real office never mentioned fees. Why the rush?
scenes.speech: Congratulations, it says. You have won an award! Submit your Aadhaar number and a five hundred rupee processing fee within twenty-four hours, or the award goes to someone else. The display name says Scholarship Office, and the logo looks right. Meera's finger hovers over Pay fee. But the real office never mentioned fees. Why the rush?
scenes.dialogue: Wait. Why would a scholarship charge a fee?

scenes.label: Show original
scenes.title: The name can lie.
scenes.caption: Her brother Arjun shows her a trick. A display name is just a label; anyone can type Scholarship Office. The truth is in the raw headers, under Show original. From shows the full address behind the name. Reply-To is where answers go. Received lists the servers it passed through. And SPF and DKIM checks show whether the sending domain vouches for it.
scenes.speech: Her brother Arjun shows her a trick. A display name is just a label; anyone can type Scholarship Office. The truth is in the raw headers, under Show original. From shows the full address behind the name. Reply-To is where answers go. Received lists the servers it passed through. And S P F and D K I M checks show whether the sending domain vouches for it.
scenes.dialogue: So the name can lie. The headers can't hide as easily.

scenes.label: Flag the clues
scenes.title: Look for several clues.
scenes.caption: Your turn. Open the raw headers and flag every field that doesn't match the real office. Leave ordinary fields like the date alone. One clue alone doesn't prove a scam, so look for several, and let each flag have a reason. Careful: the display name matching isn't evidence. Anyone can type a name.
scenes.dialogue: Four clues, not one. Then I'm sure.

scenes.label: Verify and report
scenes.title: Verify, then report.
scenes.caption: Four clues point the same way: a lookalike domain, replies going elsewhere, an unrelated server, and failed checks. Still, Meera verifies. She calls the number on the official website, not the one in the email. No fees, the office says. She tells her parents, reports the email as phishing and warns her classmates. Never send an Aadhaar number through an email link.
scenes.dialogue: Verified. It's phishing, and now everyone knows.

scenes.label: A happier ending
scenes.title: Real email. Real award.
scenes.caption: A week later, a real email arrives from youngscientists.cyberpur.example. Meera checks the headers out of habit: every field matches. She's won the scholarship, and there's no fee at all. The office thanks her for reporting the fake, which reached twenty other applicants. Your turn: help Meera inspect more email headers!
